concept.name: Shadow trading
concept.definition: A prospective test that generates and records production-intended orders alongside a live process but does not route those orders for execution.
concept.intuition: It is part of the machinery that converts strategy instructions into simulated positions, cash flows, and performance.
concept.mechanics: Feed the production data stream through frozen logic, retain intended order timestamps and quantities, and compare them with executable quotes and actual system latency.
concept.failure_modes: Simplified timing, liquidity, fee, borrow, funding, or corporate-action assumptions can make simulated results unattainable live.
concept.misconceptions: A detailed simulator reduces modeling error but cannot reproduce every queue event or future market condition.
concept.example: A shadow strategy logs a 10:00:00 buy and later measures the ask available when the order would have reached the venue.
